h1: Blending Play Equipment with Green Spaces

props.title: Blending Play Equipment with Green Spaces
props.summaryText: How to bring play into a park or garden without turning it into a rubber-covered yard: siting, layout, colours, surfaces and planting that let equipment and greenery work together.
props.author: rohan-mehta
props.imageAlt: FunPlay team members gathered outdoors at a school site

takeaways.text: Place equipment in clusters around existing trees and open lawns rather than paving one large area.
Respect tree roots: keep foundations and surfacing away from the root zone of mature trees.
Earthy and green colours, wood-finish panels and nature-inspired designs sit better in gardens.
Use turf with a shock pad or rubber in natural tones where you need impact protection.

faq.q: How do you add a playground to a garden without losing greenery?
faq.a: Use smaller clusters of equipment placed around existing trees and lawns, keep the root zones of mature trees free of foundations and hard surfaces, choose surfaces such as turf with a shock pad in safety zones, and plant around the edges.

faq.q: What playground equipment suits a garden or park setting?
faq.a: Nature-inspired structures, wood-finish towers and equipment in earthy or green colours blend well with planting. Swings, climbing nets and balance trails also sit naturally in green spaces.

faq.q: Can playground equipment be installed under trees?
faq.a: Equipment can be placed near trees for shade, but keep foundations out of the root zone of mature trees, check for dead or brittle branches overhead, and avoid trees with thorns, toxic fruit or heavy fruit fall.
